source.title: CLIPErase: Efficient Unlearning of Visual-Textual Associations in CLIP
source.authors: Tian-Yu Yang; Lisen Dai; Zheyuan Liu; Xiang-Qi Wang; Meng Jiang; Yapeng Tian; Xiang-Liang Zhang

record.file_problem: Whole paper and appendices are present; the main result tables are flattened in places, and the text gives some CLIPErase values in prose where the table entry is missing.
record.tranche_reason: Applies and evaluates unlearning in a new setting: visual-textual associations in CLIP and related vision-language models. It reports forgetting and retention outcomes, but does not test the listed recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The study measures outcomes after unlearning. It does not fine-tune unlearned models on recovery data, ablate an activation direction, quantize weights, or test prompt-based recovery. Attention and embedding visualizations are not tests of those recovery mechanisms.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It proposes CLIPErase for CLIP, a vision-language embedding model rather than an LLM, and reports only forget-set and retain-set accuracy or recall after unlearning. It runs no relearning, ablation, quantization or prompting attack, so no result bears on whether unlearning is shallow or recoverable. Reporting its own method's forgetting against baselines is method performance, not a test of version A, whose defining part is that simple attacks fail. It cites Who's Harry Potter only in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that CLIPErase removes targeted visual-textual associations and preserves retain-set performance across zero-shot, retrieval and diffusion tasks, and that it generalizes to BLIP. They do not test recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: A multimodal CLIP unlearning objective combining forget-set cross-modal misalignment, retain-set contrastive alignment, and consistency regularization; it is not an LLM unlearning recipe. The text does not describe recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary across dataset and task: CLIPErase reports near-zero forget accuracy on the zero-shot datasets, while Flickr30K retrieval results retain nonzero forget-set recall and show lower retain-set recall than the original model. Forget-set class also affects results in the appendix.

fits_no_version.finding: CLIPErase brings CLIP forget-set zero-shot accuracy to roughly 0% while keeping retain-set accuracy (CIFAR-100: 0.00 forget vs 90.99 retain). Flickr30K forget-set recall stays above zero. BLIP reaches 0.00 forget vs 83.12 retain. No robustness-to-recovery test is run.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning methods for vision-language embedding models can suppress targeted image-text associations on standard metrics while keeping retain-set performance; robustness to recovery is not established.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The paper notes a lack of dedicated multimodal unlearning benchmarks. The Conceptual 12M experiments use a 120,000-pair sample rather than the full dataset. No recovery attacks are tested, and no uncertainty estimates are reported. Some CLIPErase Table 2 entries are missing in the provided flattened table and are reported in prose.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row cap is reached. Omitted Table 3 comparator-method retrieval results, BLIP/Table 5 results, diffusion detection/Table 6 results, ablation results, and appendix class-variance, patch-size, and scalability tables/figures. These are not needed to record the primary CLIP CLIPErase results and the main Table 2 comparisons; omitted sections are Tables 3-11 and Figures 3-7, except the CLIPErase Table 3 values included above.

untested.parts: Not tested in LLMs. In CLIP, only forget and retain performance is reported, and no attack is attempted to recover the knowledge.
No direction ablation. Attention and t-SNE visualizations do not test blocking versus deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, cross-lingual or in-context recovery.
CLIPErase is a new method, but its resistance to any attack is not evaluated.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T3 and the version A labels are rejected. A study that reports only post-unlearning accuracy, without any recovery attempt, cannot bear on shallow unlearning, and the system is CLIP rather than an LLM. Extraction errors: r41-r44 are mislabelled ENMN rows and are actually CLIPErase values. The Conceptual 12M CLIPErase prose values conflict with the Table 2 values. CLIPErase entries for CIFAR-100 are present in the table.

versions.untested_parts: Tests targeted performance and retained-task performance after unlearning in vision-language models, not LLMs. Does not test whether simple attacks recover the knowledge.
No recovery fine-tuning or relearning set.
No activation-direction ablation or test of whether knowledge is blocked from access rather than deleted.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery tests.
CLIPErase is proposed as an unlearning method, but the study does not test resistance to the recovery attacks in the claim.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-100 and Conceptual 12M zero-shot tasks with CLIPErase
reader_labels.reason: Forget-set accuracy is reported as 0.00%, 0.3%, or 0.4%, while retain-set performance is maintained or higher than the original CLIP reference (r21-r24, r45-r48). These outcomes support the unlearning and retention portion of A, not its attack-resistance component.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Forget-set retrieval remains nonzero and retain-set recall is below the original CLIP reference across the reported metrics (r49-r60).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Gradient Ascent comparator on CIFAR-100 and Conceptual 12M
reader_labels.reason: Some target scores fall substantially, but retain-set accuracy is also very low in these reported settings (r05-r08, r29-r32).
